layers.note: A small tree in the understory of Douglas-fir forest.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,200 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on slopes as well as flats.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −2 °C, gone by −6 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −18 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −26 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 14 to 25 °C; gone below 12 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: A humid climate: a moisture index from about 0.55 (gone by 0.4), wet winters filling the soil through a dry summer.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Pacific dogwood grows from south-west British Columbia to southern California, in the Coast Ranges and the Sierra Nevada (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
